In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, while the translation of research evidence for use in lawmaking is a high priority, it is not the only priority, nor the only way that researchers can help policy makers.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the translation of research evidence is more than a matter of finding the right evidence to fit a given policy problem.
the evidence base for policy innovation is broader than is often recognized.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the translation of research evidence is an important goal, there is more to be said about the role of evidence in public health law.
evidence can be used to help craft even very innovative policy, even when direct evidence about the innovation itself is unavailable.
